title: ZIA provisioning methods and which authentication each allows

prose.text: Provisioning (getting users into the Zscaler database) and authentication (identifying traffic) are separate choices, but not independent ones. {{five-methods}} {{recommendation}}

prose.label: Directory synchronization.
prose.text: {{directory-sync-needs-reach}} What it does once connected is in [[zia.ad-integration.directory-sync]].

prose.label: SAML and SCIM
prose.text: are covered in [[zia.ad-integration.saml-auto-provisioning]] and [[zia.scim]]. The org-level migration switch from directory sync to SCIM is [[zia.authentication.settings:scim-migration-flag]], with its reversibility question open in [[zia.authentication.settings]].

five-methods.statement: The service supports five provisioning methods: Identity Federation using SCIM, SAML, the Hosted User Database, synchronization with a directory server, and the Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB).

quotes: the 5 supported provisioning methods: Identity Federation using SCIM, SAML, Hosted User Database, synchronization with a directory server, and Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB)

recommendation.statement: Zscaler recommends SCIM for provisioning and SAML identity federation for authentication. Directory synchronization is recommended if SAML is not feasible and the organization has more than 100 users; the hosted user database if SAML or SCIM are not feasible and the organization has up to 100 users.

quotes: Zscaler recommends deploying SCIM for provisioning and Identity Federation using SAML for authentication.
Passwords are never synchronized. If SAML isn't feasible, Zscaler recommends this method for organizations with more than 100 users.
Upload user information to the database manually through a CSV import or a ZAB. If SAML or SCIM aren't feasible, Zscaler recommends this method for organizations with up to 100 users.

auth-pairing.statement: Each provisioning method allows only some authentication methods. SCIM: SAML only. Hosted User Database: passwords (default), Kerberos, one-time link, one-time token. Directory server synchronization: LDAP BIND, one-time link, one-time token. ZAB: Hosted User Database, SAML, LDAP BIND, one-time link, one-time token.

quotes: Users and groups are provisioned via APIs. SAML is the only supported authentication method.

If SAML or SCIM aren't feasible, Zscaler recommends this method for organizations with up to 100 users.Following are the supported authentication methods:Passwords (Default)KerberosOne-Time LinkOne-Time Token
To learn more, see About LDAP User Synchronization.Following are the supported authentication methods:LDAP BINDOne-Time LinkOne-Time Token
While the ZAB is being used for provisioning, you cannot enable SCIM on any IdP.Following are the supported authentication methods:Hosted User DatabaseSAMLLDAP BINDOne-Time LinkOne-Time Token

directory-sync-needs-reach.statement: Directory server synchronization requires the firewall to allow the Zscaler service to reach the directory server, with read-only access to the directory. Passwords are never synchronized.

quotes: Configure firewall to allow the Zscaler service to synchronize with directory server.The Zscaler service must have read-only access to the directory.

zab-outbound.statement: The ZAB is a virtual appliance that imports users from an AD or LDAP server without requiring inbound connections to the directory server: it opens a long-living outbound tunnel to the Zscaler Central Authority, downloads the organization's authentication profile and synchronizes on demand or as scheduled. It can be used only to provision, alongside SAML or Kerberos authentication, or also to authenticate with LDAP.

quotes: without requiring inbound connections to your directory server.
The ZAB can be used solely as a provisioning tool in conjunction with another authentication mechanism, such as SAML or Kerberos.
the ZAB opens a long-living secure outbound tunnel to the Zscaler Central Authority (CA).
It downloads the authentication profile configuration of your organization from the CA
It synchronizes user information from the directory server to the Zscaler cloud on demand or as scheduled.
The Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB) is a virtual appliance that you can use to provision as well as authenticate users.
You can use the ZAB to automatically import user information from an Active Directory (AD) or a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server to the Zscaler database,
Alternatively, it can be used for authentication using LDAP with SSL client certificates.

zab-exclusions.statement: When the ZAB provisions and SAML authenticates, only the primary IdP in the Admin Console can have SAML auto-provisioning enabled, and SCIM cannot be enabled on any IdP while the ZAB is used for provisioning.

quotes: only the primary IdP in the Zscaler Admin Console can have SAML auto-provisioning enabled. While the ZAB is being used for provisioning, you cannot enable SCIM on any IdP.

pairing-consequences.statement: Under the pairing table a tenant that provisions by SCIM can authenticate with SAML only, and directory server synchronization offers LDAP BIND, one-time link and one-time token, so it offers neither SAML nor Kerberos.
pairing-consequences.conditions: Reads the pairing table as exhaustive: a method not listed for a provisioning method is not offered with it.

zab-to-scim-cutover.statement: A tenant moving from ZAB provisioning to SCIM cannot run both at once: SCIM cannot be enabled on any IdP while the ZAB is used for provisioning, so the move is a cutover rather than an overlap.
zab-to-scim-cutover.conditions: Assumes the ZAB is still the provisioning method until it is stopped; a ZAB used only to authenticate is not covered by the exclusion as worded.
